after.title: Forward compatibility of close.git checkpoints via team.minPackageVersion
after.context: Checkpoints whose frozen close inputs include close.git (written from 6.5.0) are reported as unauthorized transitions by 6.4.x runtimes, and a 6.4.x retry would raise CHECKPOINT_CONFLICT. Scopes and project.json are tracked, so mixed-version teams are affected (kyro qa M2, debt-3). Shipped runtimes cannot be changed; 6.4.x already warns in kyro doctor when the runtime is older than project.json team.minPackageVersion.
after.decision: Use the existing team.minPackageVersion as the compatibility signal: when a close writes close.git and the shared policy is unset or below the release that introduced close.git, print an advisory (text and structured warning) recommending team.minPackageVersion >= that release; never edit project.json automatically. Document the break in CHANGELOG, docs/teams.md, and docs/sprint-close-checkpoints.md; no doc may claim the change is fully schema-compatible without this caveat.
consequences: Teams that follow the advisory get a doctor WARN on outdated 6.4.x runtimes before they misread history.
Teams that ignore it can still see false tamper reports on 6.4.x; documented, not prevented.
No new marker or schema version; backward compatibility is unchanged.
alternatives: New writer-version marker: rejected, 6.4.x runtimes cannot read it.
Automatically raise team.minPackageVersion on close: rejected, silently changes shared team policy.
Accept the risk with docs only: rejected, gives mixed-version teams no machine signal.
